authority: CLAUDE.md §8.4 and §13.4 (no Phase 8 activity, including preparatory drafting, before the budget gate passes; absent budget artifacts are a blocking gate failure, not a hold state), §8.1 and §8.3 (the repository computes no lump-sum figure and invents none), §12.1 to §12.4 (reviewability, the four status categories, explicit gate failure on a missing mandatory input) and §15 (explicit failure over fabricated completion).
§17.1.4 and §17.6.3 are why no gate_result.json is written here: gate evaluation belongs to the scheduler and gate results to the gate evaluator.
§9.1 and §9.4 make this report and its decision record the durable form of what was found.

The ticket 'Candidate Part B and the blind baseline' in plans/dev_graph_demo_tickets.md supplies the four acceptance criteria. The blind lane is out-of-band QA (harness/HARNESS.md): advisory, never a runtime gate.
question_asked: Does the demo reach a candidate Part B and a blind baseline: Phase 8 released or its blocking gate recorded; candidate version 1 imported as a document snapshot with passages linked by span; a blind report carrying the candidate hash, profile version and assessor pin; and the leakage guard confirming no historical-feedback item entered the package?
answer: One of four. Criterion 1 is met on its second branch: the blocking gate is recorded, and Phase 8 has produced nothing. The other three are not met. Criterion 4 names the package built around candidate version 1, and no such package exists; the guard did run clean over the 6 blind packages the demo world holds, which is a real check but not the one the criterion asks for. Criteria 2 and 3 are blocked for two separate reasons that must not be conflated. Criterion 2 is blocked upstream. BIODIV-01 is a lump-sum RIA, the operator has not run the external Lump Sum Budget Planner, received/ is empty, so gate_09 fails and every Phase 8 node is frozen. No Part B text exists, and drafting one here would be the §13.4 violation the gate exists to prevent. Criterion 3 is blocked by a defect this ticket found. The blind lane's dev-graph document route cannot feed either real instrument profile: the route materialises one sub-section per section, named for the section, while the RIA rubrics anchor on B.1.1 to B.3.2 and the MSCA-PF rubrics on 1.1 to 3.2. The evidence-pack anchor map fails closed, so a bound RIA report through the guarded route is unreachable today, Part B or no Part B. Criterion 3 would still fail after the operator's planner run and a full Phase 8. That is the finding this ticket exists to surface.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Phase 8 reaches released, or its blocking gate is recorded.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Recorded here, not as a gate_result.json (§17.6.3; no node was dispatched). What is recorded is what the gate's own predicates return on the repository as it stands. docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ holds no file, so dir_non_empty fails: that is g08_p02, the predicate whose failure triggers the hard block. validation/ is likewise empty (g08_p03). No budget_gate_assessment.json exists (g08_p08). phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/ holds its .gitkeep placeholder and nothing else, so there is no gate_result.json, against 6 gate_result.json files for phases 1 to 6. runner.dag_scheduler._HARD_BLOCK_GATE is still gate_09_budget_consistency and PHASE_8_NODE_IDS still names all six Phase 8 nodes. Phase 8 has produced nothing: phase_outputs/phase8_drafting_review/ and its three section_drafts directories hold 5 .gitkeep placeholders and no other file, and docs/tier5_deliverables/ holds 6 .gitkeep placeholders and no other file. Checked by tests/test_demo_candidate_blind_baseline.py TestThePhase8BlockIsRecorded.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Candidate version 1 is a document snapshot with state imported, with passages linked by span.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: No document record exists: read_document_records returns the empty list and docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/documents/ does not exist. The demo snapshot holds 116 nodes of 7 types and no artifact_version node, so resolve_document refuses 'DEMO-BIODIV-2027_part_b' with 'no document snapshot named ... in the current build'. The cause is the lump-sum budget gate, not the import machinery: §13.4 forbids drafting the Part B this criterion would import, and that prohibition binds this report's author as much as the runner. The import route itself is verified against a synthetic RIA-shaped document in a temporary graph root, where the record lands under state 'imported' and the materialised sections carry the passage id and version. Checked by TestNoCandidateVersionExists and TestTheImportRouteWorks.
acceptance_criteria.status_if_run_later: Unresolved until the operator runs the planner and Phase 8 is dispatched.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The blind report carries the candidate hash, profile version and assessor pin, and is labelled complete or partial.
acceptance_criteria.disposition: not met, blocked by finding F1
acceptance_criteria.evidence: No blind report was written, and none could be. Two blocks stand. The first is criterion 2: there is nothing to assess. The second is independent of it and survives Phase 8. Through the guarded document route under harness/profiles/ria_default.json, build_blind_evidence succeeds — snapshot, blind-view package, leakage guard, materialised candidate — and assess_candidate then fails closed with EvidencePackError: anchor sub-section B.1.1 is not present in excellence_section.json, which has only excellence_section. materialise_candidate writes exactly one sub-section per passage and names it for the section; all six RIA rubrics anchor on B.1.1 to B.3.2. The same mismatch holds for MSCA-PF, whose nine rubrics anchor on 1.1 to 3.2 against the same three section ids. Reproduced on a synthetic RIA-shaped document by TestTheDocumentRouteCannotFeedTheRiaProfile. The three report fields this criterion names are reachable today through the directory route, which grades section artifacts an operator supplies and would produce a labelled report carrying all three. That route is not what the ticket asks for: it specifies the assessment runs 'through the blind pre-evaluation view', which is the document route, and the directory route carries no package, is not covered by the leakage guard, and refuses to stamp an intake. So the criterion fails on the route it names, not on the grader.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The leakage guard confirms no historical-feedback item entered the package.
acceptance_criteria.disposition: not met as stated; the guard ran clean over the packages that exist
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The demo world holds 36 evidence packages, 6 of them built under the blind_pre_evaluation view (tasks T1.1, T3.1 and T4.1, each at two package ids). assert_no_leakage was run over all 6, rebuilt from their stored manifest.json and package.json, and every one is clean: no item of type assessment, finding or change_request, and no item carrying any of the HISTORICAL_FEEDBACK_TAGS. The two T4.1 packages each carry one policy_forbidden exclusion, MS6 under traversal_not_permitted:validated_by, which is the view policy refusing a traversal rather than the guard refusing an item. The guard's negative is unconditional on this branch for a stronger reason than the walk: the demo world contains no document record at all, so no document tags exist to leak, and the ESR intake records availability not_applicable. Two things have not been checked. The first is the package this criterion names, the one built around candidate version 1, because no such package exists. The second is weightier and is recorded as F6: across all 6 blind packages the item types are task 50, participant 22, work_package 6, source 4 and deliverable 2, and passage, claim and commitment are each 0. A historical-feedback tag rides on a document's passages, claims and commitments, so these packages cannot carry the leak the guard looks for. The clean pass is correct and is not evidence that the guard would catch a leak here. Checked by TestTheLeakageGuardIsCleanOnTheDemoWorld, which also plants an item to show the guard firing.

the_esr_intake.why_not_applicable: The demo is a demonstration, not a submission. Nothing was submitted, so no Evaluation Summary Report exists and none can. not_applicable states that, where unavailable would state that a report exists and was not obtained. The intake module declares availability and never infers it, so the field had to be set explicitly: prior_submission false on its own would have stored unknown.
the_esr_intake.why_it_is_written_now: Writing the intake is not Phase 8 activity. §13.4 covers the Phase 8 substeps — drafting, assembly, evaluator review, revision — and this is an out-of-band dev-graph record of what is known about an ESR. It fixes the document identity the eventual import must use, which is what makes that import checkable rather than negotiable. The builder never reads the intake directory, so the demo snapshot id is unchanged at sha256:93b18297a8703157e77e08d1a3c97abd240f752b63b711ca0b3037f6141bd836.
the_esr_intake.cost_of_writing_it_early: An intake record is immutable. If Phase 8 later produces Part B under a document id other than DEMO-BIODIV-2027_part_b, this record is wrong and a new intake id is required. The id follows the demo project label the snapshot summary already carries, which is the only project identity this branch has: the acronym in Tier 3 is Unresolved.

the_gate.human_step_outstanding: The operator runs the external Lump Sum Budget Planner against docs/tier3_project_instantiation/integration/budget_request.json and places the response in received/. Until then the gate's failure is the correct output, and no Phase 8 substep may begin.

what_was_checked_and_how: The Phase 8 block: the gate_09 predicates run directly as pure functions over the real repository, with no node dispatched and no gate result written. The frozen set is read from runner.run_context.PHASE_8_NODE_IDS and the hard-block gate from runner.dag_scheduler._HARD_BLOCK_GATE, then cross-checked against the manifest gate_registry entry and its blocking_edges.

The absence of a candidate: runner.dev_graph.documents.read_document_records over the real repository, and harness.blind_assessment.resolve_document over the real demo snapshot built by build_snapshot.

The leakage guard: each stored package under docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/packages/ is rebuilt as a Package from its manifest.json and package.json, filtered to view blind_pre_evaluation, and passed to assert_no_leakage. All 6 pass. The guard is also shown to fire on a planted item, so a pass is not a vacuous pass.

The document-route defect: a synthetic RIA-shaped document carrying the three profile-required section ids is imported into a copy of tests/fixtures/dev_graph_synthetic under tmp_path, blind evidence is built under the real harness/profiles/ria_default.json, and assess_candidate is called with a stub assessor. It raises EvidencePackError naming the missing anchor. Nothing is written into docs/ by this check.

The intake record: written through runner.dev_graph.intake.record_esr_intake, re-read through read_esr_intake, and shown immutable — the same content again is a no-op, and different content under the same id is refused.

Anonymity: py -3.10 -m runner.leakage_scan over 164 files in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 and the vault, this report and its decision record included. No new leak. The 11 recorded pre-existing leaks in the 22 September purge record are unchanged.

findings.severity: blocking for the blind lane's guarded route
findings.finding: The dev-graph document route cannot feed either real instrument profile. materialise_candidate writes one sub-section per passage and gives it the section's own id; the RIA rubrics anchor on B.1.1, B.1.2, B.2.1, B.2.2, B.3.1 and B.3.2, and the MSCA-PF rubrics on 1.1 to 3.2. build_evidence_pack fails closed on the missing anchor. The only profile the route can serve is one whose rubric anchors equal its section ids, which describes the synthetic syn_graph profile in tests/harness/test_blind_leakage.py and no shipped profile.
findings.why_it_was_not_caught_before: The document route's tests use the synthetic profile, where anchor and section id coincide. The RIA and MSCA-PF profile tests use the directory route with a candidate built from the rubric anchors. No test crossed the two. This is what handoff stage 7 was for.
findings.fix_shape: Either a document record declares its sub-sections and materialise_candidate preserves them, or the profile declares how a section's passage maps onto its anchors. The first keeps the anchor map fail-closed and puts the structure where the drafter already knows it; the second changes no document schema. The choice is not this ticket's to make: it changes what a document snapshot is.

findings.finding: An ESR intake can be stamped on a blind report only through the document route: _check_intake refuses an intake when the candidate is a directory, because a directory names no document. While F1 stands, the demo's not_applicable availability cannot reach any RIA blind report, so criteria 3 and 4 cannot be satisfied by the same report.
findings.fix_shape: None of its own. Fixing F1 resolves it.

findings.finding: record_esr_intake requires a submission_id matching a plain-identifier pattern, with no way to declare that no submission exists. The demo was never submitted and never will be, so the record carries the sentinel NOT_SUBMITTED. The sentinel is a declaration of absence, not an invented identifier, and cannot be mistaken for a submission number.
findings.fix_shape: Make submission_id optional when esr_availability is not_applicable, or add a declared absence value. Either way it stays declared and never inferred, which is the module's existing rule.

findings.finding: Phase 8 has produced nothing, so there is no candidate version 1. This is the gate working, not a defect. The outstanding step is the operator's: run the external planner and place the response in received/.

The demo world's 6 blind packages hold no passage, claim or commitment item: the item types are task 50, participant 22, work_package 6, source 4 and deliverable 2. The builder derives those three types from document records, and the demo has none. A historical-feedback tag is stamped on a document's passages, claims and commitments, so no item in these packages could carry one. assert_no_leakage passing over them is correct and tells a reader nothing about whether a real Part B package would be clean.
findings.disposition: recorded; it is why criterion 4's box stays open
findings.fix_shape: None at the code level. The check becomes meaningful when a document record exists, which is criterion 2.

findings.finding: The demo's 6 blind packages are all labelled incomplete under the budget of 3000 that ticket 8 used. assert_no_leakage is indifferent to completeness, but build_blind_evidence refuses an incomplete package outright, so the budget a real Part B assessment needs is higher than the one the snapshot ticket demonstrated with. Ticket 8 recorded 5.4k to 21.9k for the mandatory set, and the blind lane's own default package budget is 200000.
findings.disposition: recorded; no change made, because no real package is built yet

Criterion 2, candidate version 1, until the operator runs the planner and Phase 8 is dispatched.
Criterion 3, the blind report, until F1 is fixed as well.
Criterion 4 as stated, until a package exists around candidate version 1.

authored_by: Implementation of the ticket 'Candidate Part B and the blind baseline'. No runner phase was dispatched. The runtime made no Claude invocation. No gate result was written.
note: Three of the four criteria are not met, and this report says so rather than narrowing the criteria to fit. §15 prefers an explicit failure to a fabricated completion. One block is a human step the ticket always depended on. The other is a defect in the lane the ticket was written to exercise, and it would have failed the criterion even with Part B in hand.
